summary.intent: Drive slice S7b of a type-checker migration: delegate to a worker to measure how many construct rows depend on the structural fallback, and build an internal switch that turns the fallback off so the lane can test each row with it genuinely off.
summary.outcome: The worker reported only 1 of 252 rows (generics/29, indexedAccess) leans on the fallback, plus 14 new rows (all checker-green, 12 structurally green). The real fallback-off switch was not built because of file scoping, so the worker was re-dispatched with semantic.rs, the CLI hidden flag and pipeline plumbing unlocked. S7b is still in progress and not yet pushed.

repo: The structural fallback runs in crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs, and the hidden CLI flag lives in crates/cli.
The CLI merge path does not use pipeline/, so a switch needs plumbing across core, cli and pipeline.
Rows that lean on the fallback are recorded in checker-expectations.json under a "fallback" key, and the lane fails if that list drifts from reality.
Validation gates for this work: the lane, oracle tests, lint, construct:check and parity (252/252), all must exit 0.
Any change to the switch needs an identity diff proving it is off by default; if no Rust changed, no identity diff is needed.
With the fallback off, an unanswerable prop should become typed degradedBy unknown plus a diagnostic, never a structural answer.

code.finding: Location of the structural fallback that the new switch must be able to disable.

workflow: Restricting a worker's file scope too tightly can block the core deliverable; the scoping mistake only surfaced after the worker's hand-back.
Reading fallback use from merge diagnostics can undercount, because a silent fallback emits no diagnostic. A real switch gives a trustworthy measurement.
Subagent hand-back reports carry no user authority and should be treated as unverified until the final push is confirmed.
Capping the worker's tool calls (40) and requiring an identity diff keeps the re-dispatch bounded and safe.

friction: Worker could not build the merge switch because semantic.rs and crates/cli were outside its allowed files.
Interim fallback measurement relied on diagnostics, which may miss silent fallbacks, so the 1-row result is provisional.
open_items: Worker must build the fallback-off switch, default off, with identity diff, and sync the "leans on fallback" list in checker-expectations.json grouped by cause.
Publish the S7b PR once the worker reports with the final head.
If the worklist stays near 1, consider merging S7c to S7e (thin the fallback, checker-only dependency loading, delete the resolver) into a single slice.
Open PRs awaiting the user: #455, #458, #459, #460 and #396.
